the dispatch safety gate cannot tell 'this row writes here' from 'this row mentions this path', so an honest spec is refused and a vague one passes. Censused 2026-09-02 on d49964e: 20 of 125 spec files return verdict refuse. Causes: state-schema.json 8, diagnose 6, evidence/ 5, claims 5, design/ 3, then singletons. The first two causes are legitimate -- that IS the claim surface. But 'diagnose' mostly matches the FILENAME bin/perry-diagnose rather than the /perry diagnose pipeline the hook means; 'design/' matches a spec CITING design/DESIGN-NNN rather than writing into it; and 'evidence/' matches a spec declaring its own evidence output, which every dispatched row has. Live instance: TASK-263's spec was refused solely because its Files in scope and Deliverable name perry/evidence/2026-09/TASK-263-result.md, the file the row exists to produce. The pressure this creates is the dangerous part -- the cheapest way to pass is to stop naming the path, and .perry/hook.md says in its own words that rewording to pass is the one thing a gate must never reward. Same defect class as impl_refs counting a design id by text match (TASK-282): a literal matcher standing in for intent. Candidate fixes: distinguish a write-target section from a citation, or scope the fragments that name Perry's own state dirs to foreign roots only

dispatching a subagent WITHOUT worktree isolation lets it switch the shared working tree to its own branch, so the PMO's concurrent writes land there too -- and a 'git add -A' in the agent's commit would sweep them into its code commit. Observed live 2026-09-02: TASK-247 was dispatched as a claude-subagent with the instruction to create coding/task-247-config-predicate; the shared tree is now ON that branch, and every PMO write made after dispatch (TASK-212 next, TASK-282 depends, TASK-263 spec and evidence, two intake rows) is uncommitted on it. Nothing is lost and git makes it separable by path -- PMO state is perry/ plus .perry/events.jsonl, the agent's work is bin/ and tests/ -- but the separation is manual and it is only obvious to whoever knows both happened. work/reference/dispatch.md tells the agent to work on a feature branch and says nothing about tree isolation, while git-boundaries.md's whole premise is that one agent must not silently rewrite another's lane. The Agent tool supports isolation: worktree; the dispatch procedure should either require it or state why the shared tree is acceptable

10 of this project's 27 V4 closures carry a rung no checker can confirm was earned. Censused 2026-09-02 on d49964e with perry-lint --reviews: v4-close-without-verdict 10, verdict-malformed 9, criteria-unbounded 8, review-rounds-exhausted 1, across 12 review files and 15 named tasks. The board reports 183 closures by rung V2 3 / V3 146 / V4 27 / V5 7, so 37% of the V4 population closed with no evidence document carrying a verdict block that names the row. V4's whole content is that a FRESH reviewer ran against WRITTEN criteria -- neither half producible by the session that wrote the code -- so a V4 closure whose verdict cannot be read is a rung claimed rather than run, which is the exact wording perry-lint uses. The project's own verification statistics therefore overstate what was verified, and the standup renders that same by_rung breakdown as if all 27 were equal. Only 2 of the 15 named tasks are still open (TASK-067 P0 blocked, TASK-095 P1 review), so this is mostly a HISTORICAL record-quality problem rather than live work -- but it is also the number a future phase retro would quote. Candidate actions: decide whether the 10 are re-reviewable or should be restated at the rung actually evidenced, and whether close-task should refuse a V4 whose verdict block does not parse rather than warning after the fact

a fixture test reads the LIVE repository's event log, so a PMO prose edit reddens the suite. Measured 2026-09-02 on b93736d. tests/test_parsers.py test_locked_design_without_impl_rows_is_flagged asserts the fixture's pending_handoff is ['DESIGN-001']; it now returns [] because the fixture's DESIGN-001 has impl_refs 2. The 2 come from Perry's OWN .perry/events.jsonl -- the 'next TASK-282' event at 12:07:37 and the 'next TASK-212' event at 13:38:27, both of which merely MENTION the string DESIGN-001 in their prose. THE MECHANISM: impl_refs (viewer/parsers.py around 3298-3311) walks UP TO FOUR PARENT DIRECTORIES looking for .perry/events.jsonl when the caller passes no project_root. The fixture at tests/fixtures/sample-project has a .perry/ directory but no events.jsonl in it, so the walk climbs to tests/fixtures, then tests/, then the repository root, and reads the live log. The code comment says the bounded walk 'stays for the callers that pass no project_root at all, where a guess still beats no log' -- this is that guess being wrong. TWO DEFECTS, not one. (1) TEST ISOLATION: a fixture must not be able to read the host repository's state; giving the fixture its own empty .perry/events.jsonl would stop the walk at the fixture, and is probably the minimal fix. (2) The upward walk itself is a cross-project read that no caller asked for. Same defect family as TASK-282, and this is its strongest evidence yet: impl_refs' text matching does not merely misreport within a project, it LEAKS ACROSS PROJECT BOUNDARIES. Note for whoever fixes it: do NOT resolve this by rewording the PMO rows that mention DESIGN-001. The prose is correct and the finding it records is real; the test is what is wrong
